title: Cells and Cell Theory
seo_title: Grade 6 Cells Worksheets: Cell Theory, Unicellular and Multicellular Organisms, Microscopes
standard_text: Conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of cells; either one cell or many different numbers and types of cells.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on cells and cell theory (NGSS MS-LS1-1): unicellular and multicellular organisms, types of cells, microscopes and total magnification. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: All living things are made of cells.
key_sub: Some organisms are one cell; others are made of trillions of cells of many types. Microscopes let us see them.
body_html:
How to think about it

The cell theory says:

  1. All living things are made of one or more cells.
  2. The cell is the basic unit of life.
  3. New cells come from existing cells.

Unicellular organisms (bacteria, yeast, amoebas) are a single cell. Multicellular organisms (plants, animals, mushrooms) are made of many cells, often of different types, such as nerve, muscle and blood cells. Each cell type has a shape that fits its job.

Most cells are too small to see, so we use a microscope. Total magnification = eyepiece × objective (10× × 40× = 400×).

Example

Is yeast unicellular or multicellular?

Yeast is one cell.

Answer: unicellular

Example

A 10× eyepiece and a 100× objective give what magnification?

10 × 100

Answer: 1,000×

Common mistakes

  • Thinking only animals are made of cells. Plants, fungi and bacteria are too.
  • Adding magnifications. Multiply them.
  • Thinking bigger organisms have bigger cells. They have more cells.

faq.q: What are the three parts of the cell theory?
faq.a: All living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells come from existing cells.

faq.q: What is the difference between unicellular and multicellular organisms?
faq.a: Unicellular organisms are made of one cell. Multicellular organisms are made of many cells, often of different types.

faq.q: How do you find total magnification?
faq.a: Multiply the eyepiece magnification by the objective magnification. For example, 10× × 40× = 400×.
